items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XVI, List of Answers on Terminology 182:1
items.html: There are two aspects of Nefesh and Ruach in the ten Sefirot: the first are the Nefesh and Ruach that clothe in the internal vessels, the brain, the bones, and the sinews. And the second are the Nefesh and Ruach that clothe in the external vessels of the skin and the flesh. And the reason is that there are only three vessels in the Partzuf, KHB, which are called the brain, the bones, and the sinews, in which NRN clothe. But for Haya and Yechida there are no vessels, and they only clothe within the light of the Neshama, in the vessel of the brain. And although there are two more vessels, the flesh and the skin, the lights of Ruach and Nefesh cannot descend from the bones and the sinews to them to clothe there, in order to give room for the lights of Haya and Yechida to clothe in the vessels of the brain and the bones, because these vessels of the flesh and the skin are not complete internal vessels, but only the aspect of external vessels, which are not fit to clothe the internal Nefesh and Ruach. Therefore Haya and Yechida are compelled to clothe within the light of the Neshama. And nevertheless, the vessels of the skin and the flesh receive the aspect of the illumination of Nefesh and Ruach from the Nefesh and Ruach in the internal vessels, and they are called the external Nefesh and Ruach. (Part 1, Page 986, Sub Header, "and from here").
